title: Three largest values
prompt: Write a function named top_three that takes a list of numbers holding at least three items and returns a new list with the three largest values in it, ordered from largest to smallest. Repeated values are allowed in the answer, so [5, 5, 5, 1] gives [5, 5, 5]. The original list must not be left rearranged, so sort a copy of it. Return the list, do not print it.

title: Count how often each word appears
prompt: Write a function named count_words that takes a list of words and returns a dictionary whose keys are the words and whose values are how many times each word appears in the list. Counting is case sensitive, so "a" and "A" are different keys. An empty list gives an empty dictionary. Return the dictionary, do not print it.

title: Unique values in order
prompt: Write a function named unique_sorted that takes a list of numbers and returns a new list holding each different value once, ordered from smallest to largest. An empty list gives an empty list. Return the list, do not print it.

title: Row totals of a grid
prompt: Write a function named row_totals that takes a grid, which is a list of lists of numbers, and returns a list holding the sum of each row in the same order. An empty grid gives an empty list, and an empty row gives a total of 0. Return the list, do not print it.

title: Students who passed
prompt: Write a function named passing_students that takes a dictionary whose keys are student names and whose values are their scores, and returns a list of the names whose score is 60 or more. Keep the names in the order they appear in the dictionary. An empty dictionary gives an empty list. Return the list, do not print it.
